A_target.statement:
Let $\struct {f, g}$ be a [[Definition:Galois Connection|Galois connection]] between [[Definition:Ordered Set|ordered sets]] $P$ and $Q$.
Then the [[Definition:Closed Element|closed elements]] of $P$ are exactly:
:$\set {x \in P: \map g {\map f x} = x}$

B_source.statement:
Let $c: P \to P$ be an [[Definition:Increasing Mapping|increasing]] [[Definition:Idempotent Mapping|idempotent]] mapping on an [[Definition:Ordered Set|ordered set]].
Then:
:$\map {\operatorname {Fix} } c = \Img c$

substitutions.the monotone idempotent operator: the composite of the two maps of the Galois connection

derived.the fixed point set equals the image: every closure is closed and every closed element is its own closure
derived.the order structure on fixed points: the closed elements inherit a complete lattice structure

object_map.reformulation: Recast closedness as invariance under the round trip through the connection.

validity_conditions: The composite of the two order-reversing maps of a Galois connection is monotone, since reversing twice restores the order.
It is inflationary and idempotent, which are exactly the closure operator axioms and follow from the two defining adjunction inequalities.
Idempotence is what makes the image coincide with the fixed point set; for a monotone map that is not idempotent the two can differ.
proof_plan:
$c$ is [[Definition:Increasing Mapping|increasing]] as a composite of two order-reversing maps.
From the Galois connection, $x \le \map g {\map f x}$, so $c$ is [[Definition:Inflationary Mapping|inflationary]].
From $f \circ g \circ f = f$, $c$ is [[Definition:Idempotent Mapping|idempotent]].

If $x = \map c y$ then $\map c x = \map c {\map c y} = \map c y = x$.
Hence $\Img c = \map {\operatorname {Fix} } c$.
